D&D emerged from tabletop miniature wargaming in the 1970s. Players took the roles of individual adventurers, while a referee described the world and resolved their actions. Exploration, negotiation, and improvised solutions became central parts of play alongside combat.

The hobby spread through home groups, clubs, conventions, and published adventures. Successive editions changed its rules and brought in new generations of players. Online play and streamed games later widened its audience. Its enduring appeal is creating a shared story through player decisions and dice.
